idiom_name: func make(...) -> any Protocol (static member or module-level)
implementation_notes: Swift initialisers cannot return a different type or fail with nil, so the factory is a function - a static member or a module-level function, with convenience initialisers as the class-cluster idiom - that returns an existential: func make(...) -> any Shape. Callers depend only on the protocol, and swift.org documents that boxed protocol types erase the concrete type and add an indirection - the same trade the classic Creator makes with a virtual call.
pitfalls: Existentials box and dispatch dynamically: on hot paths prefer generics (some Shape) or an enum when the set is fixed, or you pay the indirection per call.
The `any` spelling is required from Swift 5.6 and mandatory in Swift 6 language mode; code written without it stops compiling during migration.
Initialisers cannot return nil: if construction can fail, use a failable initialiser (init?) or a throwing static factory rather than returning an implicitly unwrapped optional.

variants.name: Enum with associated values plus switch
variants.idiom_name: enum Shape { case circle(r: Double), square(side: Double) } + static make + switch
variants.implementation_notes: For a closed set of products Swift's own performance guidance recommends an enum with associated values and a switch dispatch: cases are stack allocated, the switch compiles to a jump table with no pointer indirection, and adding a case makes every non-exhaustive switch a compile error. It replaces the Creator hierarchy where the variants are known ahead of time and no client module must add one.
pitfalls: An enum closes the product set: adding a case is source-breaking for exhaustive switches in other modules (consider @frozen only inside a resilient library's own control).
Each behaviour must switch over every case, so shared behaviour tends to be duplicated; a protocol extension with default implementations keeps it in one place.
Enums cannot be extended by conformance to add a case, so plugin-style extension needs the existential form instead.
